question: What is the passing criteria for CBSE Class 10 and Class 12 board examinations?
answer:
According to the official CBSE Examination Bylaws (Rule 40.1):
1. For Class 12: A candidate must secure a minimum of 33% marks separately in THEORY and 33% marks separately in PRACTICAL/Project/Internal Assessment, along with an aggregate of 33% in each subject to be declared as PASSED.
2. For Class 10: Students must obtain an overall aggregate of 33% marks (combining Theory and Internal Assessment together) in each of the five subjects.
3. Grace Marks: CBSE grants up to 5 grace marks in total to pass a borderline student failing in a single subject.
snippet: Rule 40.1: In order to be declared to have passed the Class XII examination, a candidate must obtain at least 33% marks in theory and 33% marks in practical/project separately, besides 33% marks in aggregate in each subject.

question: What is the CBSE Class 12 Computer Science syllabus and question paper design?
answer:
CBSE Class 12 Computer Science (Subject Code 083) comprises 70 Marks Theory and 30 Marks Practical:
• Unit 1: Computational Thinking and Programming - 2 (Python, Functions, Text/Binary/CSV File Handling, Data Structures like Linear List Stacks via push/pop) - 40 Marks.
• Unit 2: Computer Networks (Network topologies, transmission media, OSI vs TCP/IP, protocols HTTP/FTP/DNS, cybersecurity) - 10 Marks.
• Unit 3: Database Management (SQL DDL/DML, Primary/Foreign keys, Aggregate functions SUM/AVG/COUNT, GROUP BY, HAVING, Joins) - 20 Marks.
• Practical Component (30 Marks): Python program (8 marks), SQL queries (4 marks), Project report (8 marks), Viva voce (5 marks), Practical file (5 marks).
snippet: Unit 1: Computational Thinking and Programming - 2 covers 40 marks including recursion, text and binary files (pickle module), and stacks using Python lists with push and pop operations.

question: What are the most frequent 5-mark derivations in CBSE Class 12 Physics?
answer:
Analysis of CBSE 10-year question papers identifies the following core 5-mark derivations:
1. Gauss's Law Applications: Electric field due to an infinitely long straight wire ($E = \frac{\lambda}{2\pi \varepsilon_0 r}$) and uniformly charged thin spherical shell.
2. Current Electricity: Kirchhoff's Laws and Wheatstone Bridge balanced condition derivation ($\frac{P}{Q} = \frac{R}{S}$).
3. Wave Optics: Huygens' Wave Theory for laws of Reflection and Refraction ($n_1 \sin i = n_2 \sin r$).
4. Ray Optics: Lens Maker's Formula ($\frac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1)(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{R_2})$) and Refraction at spherical surfaces.
5. Semiconductor Electronics: V-I characteristics of p-n junction diode in forward and reverse bias, and half-wave/full-wave rectifier circuits.
snippet: Section E contains three 5-mark questions with internal choice focusing on fundamental physical derivations including Lens Maker's Formula and Gauss's Law applications.

question: What is the weightage distribution and core formulas for CBSE Class 12 Mathematics?
answer:
CBSE Class 12 Mathematics (Code 041) carries 80 Marks Theory + 20 Marks Internal Assessment:
• Calculus (35 Marks): Continuity & Differentiability, Applications of Derivatives (Maxima/Minima), Integrals (Integration by parts: $\int u v dx = u \int v dx - \int (u' \int v dx) dx$), Definite Integral Properties, and Differential Equations.
• Vectors and 3D Geometry (14 Marks): Dot product, Cross product, Shortest distance between skew lines: $d = \frac{|(\mathbf{b}_1 \times \mathbf{b}_2) \cdot (\mathbf{a}_2 - \mathbf{a}_1)|}{|\mathbf{b}_1 \times \mathbf{b}_2|}$.
• Matrices and Determinants (10 Marks): Matrix inversion ($A^{-1} = \frac{1}{|A|} \text{adj}(A)$) and solving system of linear equations using matrix method.
• Probability (8 Marks): Conditional probability, Multiplication theorem, and Bayes' Theorem: $P(E_i|A) = \frac{P(E_i)P(A|E_i)}{\sum P(E_k)P(A|E_k)}$.
snippet: Calculus dominates the blueprint with 35 marks out of 80. Mandatory 6-mark/case-study questions appear regularly on Maxima-Minima and Bayes' Theorem.

question: What are the CBSE attendance rules and mark re-evaluation procedure?
answer:
1. Attendance Requirement (Rule 13): A candidate must have minimum 75% attendance during the academic session to appear in board examinations. Shortage up to 15% can be condoned by the CBSE Chairman only on valid medical grounds or national sports participation.
2. Re-evaluation Process: Follows a strict 3-stage protocol:
   - Step 1: Verification of Marks (checking totaling errors, Rs 500/subject).
   - Step 2: Obtaining Scanned Photocopy of Evaluated Answer Book (Rs 700/subject).
   - Step 3: Re-evaluation of specific questions with textbook reference (Rs 100/question).
snippet: Rule 13.1 requires 75% minimum physical attendance. Rule 61 specifies the three-tier challenge mechanism: Verification -> Photocopy -> Re-evaluation.

question: What is the Choice Based Credit System (CBCS) and passing criteria in RTU Kota B.Tech?
answer:
Under Rajasthan Technical University (RTU) Choice Based Credit System (CBCS):
1. Total Credits: 160 credits required over 8 semesters for awarding B.Tech degree (approx. 20-22 credits per semester).
2. Theory Passing Standard: Minimum 36% marks in End-Term Examination (29 out of 80 marks) and an aggregate of 40% combining Internal (Mid-Term) and External marks.
3. Practical Passing Standard: Minimum 40% in internal and external practical assessments.
4. CGPA Formula: $\text{CGPA} = \frac{\sum_{i} (C_i \times G_i)}{\sum_{i} C_i}$, where $C_i$ is course credit and $G_i$ is grade point (S=10, A+=9, A=8.5, B+=7.5, B=6.5, C=5.5, F=0/Fail).
snippet: RTU Ordinance 10.2: Minimum passing marks in End-Term theory examination is 36%. Total minimum aggregate in theory course is 40% of maximum marks.

question: What are the RTU 5th Semester Java Project Based Learning (PBL) guidelines and evaluation criteria at Arya College?
answer:
The RTU Java PBL Course (5th Sem, Dept. of CSE, Mentor: Er. Ram Babu Buri) requires:
1. Tech Stack Mandate: Enterprise Java backend (Spring Boot 3, Java 21 LTS) coupled with relational/vector databases and modern client architecture.
2. Team Governance: Exactly 5 students per team with an appointed Team Leader, working across 5 dedicated Git feature branches.
3. Version Control Rule: Minimum 3 commits per student per week over 14 project weeks (verified via commit hash logs).
4. Evaluation Schema (100 Marks): Weekly work log submissions (20 marks), Mid-term SRS & UML review (20 marks), Final project working code & live demo (40 marks), and External Viva Voce examination (20 marks).
5. Portal Submission: Mandatory weekly report and daily work logs synced with javapbl5thsem.netlify.app.
snippet: Arya College Java PBL guidelines mandate 5 members, 5 feature branches, 3 commits/student/week, and full 14-week daily logs matching the departmental portal.

question: What are the core theory subjects and syllabus outline for RTU B.Tech CSE 5th Semester?
answer:
RTU B.Tech 5th Semester Computer Science curriculum covers 5 core theory subjects:
1. 5CS4-01: Compiler Design (Lexical Analysis, Finite Automata, Parsing LL(1), LR(0), SLR, LALR, CLR, Intermediate code generation, Three Address Code).
2. 5CS4-02: Operating Systems (CPU Scheduling FCFS/SJF/Round Robin, Synchronization Semaphores, Deadlock prevention/avoidance Banker's Algorithm, Paging & Segmentation).
3. 5CS4-03: Database Management Systems (Relational Algebra, SQL, Normalization 1NF to BCNF, Concurrency Control 2PL, ACID Transactions).
4. 5CS4-04: Analysis & Design of Algorithms (Asymptotic notations $O, \Omega, \Theta$, Divide & Conquer Merge/QuickSort, Dynamic Programming 0/1 Knapsack, Bellman-Ford, Dijkstra).
5. 5CS4-05: Software Engineering & PBL (Agile, Scrum, SRS IEEE Std 830, UML diagrams, Java enterprise development).
snippet: Semester V theory subjects include 5CS4-01 Compiler Design, 5CS4-02 Operating Systems, 5CS4-03 Database Management Systems, 5CS4-04 Analysis of Algorithms, and Java PBL.

question: What is the RTU Kota grace marks rule and back paper policy for engineering students?
answer:
According to RTU Examination Ordinances:
1. Grace Marks Rule: Maximum of 1% of the total aggregate marks of the semester can be awarded as grace marks to pass an examination. Grace marks can be distributed across a maximum of 2 subjects, provided the student clears all remaining subjects.
2. Back Paper Policy: If a student scores less than 36% in external theory or less than 40% aggregate, they are awarded an 'F' grade and must appear in the Back Paper Examination.
3. Maximum Course Duration: A student admitted to 4-year B.Tech must complete the degree within $N + 3$ years, i.e., maximum 7 academic years from initial admission.
4. Revaluation: Students can apply for copy inspection and answer book revaluation within 15 days of result declaration.
snippet: RTU Ordinance 15: Grace marks up to 1% of total aggregate marks of the examination may be awarded to a candidate failing in not more than two theory papers.

question: What is the RTU End-Term question paper pattern and internal marks distribution?
answer:
For an 80-mark End-Term Theory Exam (3 Hours Duration), RTU follows a three-section blueprint:
• Section A (10 Questions x 2 Marks = 20 Marks): Compulsory short conceptual questions covering all 5 syllabus units.
• Section B (5 Questions x 4 Marks = 20 Marks): Medium analytical questions with internal choices between units.
• Section C (4 Questions x 10 Marks = 40 Marks, attempt any 4 out of 5): Long comprehensive derivations, design algorithms, and numerical problems.
• Internal Marks (20 Marks Total): 2 Mid-Term tests of 20 marks each averaged to 10 marks, plus 10 marks for assignments, attendance, and continuous tutorial assessment.
snippet: RTU end-semester question paper consists of three parts: Part A (20 marks short compulsory), Part B (20 marks analytical), and Part C (40 marks descriptive/numerical).
